scope: Unchanged installed pg Client JavaScript evaluated with injected streams, protocol frames and controlled scheduling. No database, real transport or server qualification.
findings: Success follows injected ReadyForQuery; CommandComplete alone does not settle the simple query. Callback ordering is confirmed only under the exercised synthetic scheduling.
Backend error and non-pipeline query timeout reject before protocol-idle or transport-close evidence. Timeout initiates no cancellation or transport cutoff in this profile.
The cached transaction status remains stale between correlated protocol messages, including during a pending rollback.
Idle end sends Terminate and waits for injected close. Active non-pipeline end invokes destroy and still waits for close.
Active cancel opens a second synthetic connection and returns undefined without acknowledgment. Later target completion is injected by the fixture.
qualifications: Scenario and assertion counts overlap and must not be added into unique behavioral cases.
Controls alter source only in VM memory; their subsequent fixture disposal is not evidence of production cleanup authority.
The VM uses trusted host helpers and is not an adversarial sandbox. Its wrapper-creation timeout and finite scheduler do not prove general execution containment.
Controlled scheduling is not a full native event loop. Injected close is not a real network event or server acknowledgment.
Pool, pipeline, native, authentication, TLS, paged portals, connection timeout, actual cancellation, backend termination, RD7 and target version/provenance remain untested.
authority: D2 remains unchanged: no new post-fatal query, rollback, close, cancel or destroy. D3 server termination remains UNKNOWN. No READY, quota, host GO or production wiring acceptance.
next: Use these client semantics when reviewing an actual-driver contract; do not infer resource or server settlement from Promise rejection or cached status.
